# Fundamental Analysis: 4062.T

## 1. Executive conclusion

**Fundamental rating: Neutral.** Decision horizon 3–6 months (to ~end-April 2027).

- **Business direction: strongly positive.** 4062.T (Ibiden) is the leading domestic supplier of high-end IC package substrates, and the operating evidence in the latest half is unambiguous: H1 FY3/27 (six months to 30 Sep 2026) revenue rose 34.3% to JPY262,546m and operating profit rose 84.6% to JPY60,116m, both first-half records, driven by AI-related substrate demand and pricing [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1][doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].
- **Earnings direction: positive but decelerating in rate of change.** Management guides FY3/27 to revenue [[565.0]]bn and operating profit [[133.0]]bn, implying H2 operating margin of 24.1% versus 22.9% in H1 — a modest step-up, not a second inflection [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3].
- **Forecast position: no edge.** My base case equals management guidance for FY3/27 (because the build is H1 actual plus H2 guidance) and equals the Citi-cited consensus of [[190.0]]bn for FY3/28 operating profit. The base case does not currently provide a material forecast edge versus the available consensus for this metric.
- **Cash-flow quality: weak on a normalized basis.** H1 operating cash flow of JPY193.2bn included a JPY118.8bn increase in customer advances; excluding that, underlying operating cash flow was roughly JPY74bn against capex of JPY48.3bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9][p.10]. The FY3/28 capex plan of ~JPY350bn against ~JPY280bn of EBITDA implies negative free cash flow.
- **Balance sheet: strong today, but being consumed.** Net cash of roughly JPY258bn at 30 Sep 2026 (cash JPY420.5bn less interest-bearing debt of ~JPY162bn) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.4][p.5], against a capex programme of ~JPY350bn in FY3/28 and >JPY400bn annually thereafter [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].
- **Valuation: full.** At [[8,045]] the stock trades at [[35.9]]x FY3/28 EPS of [[224.1]] and roughly 15–16x FY3/28 EV/EBITDA, with negative normalized free cash flow. The model's fair-value range is [[6,274]]–[[8,515]] with a base of [[8,000]], i.e. approximately −1% from the current price.
- **Main catalyst (within horizon):** Q3 FY3/27 results (late January/early February 2027) and the promised decision/disclosure on Cell 7 and Cell 9 investment by end-FY3/27, which brokers identify as the next re-rating trigger [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].
- **Main risk:** the market has begun pricing a share-loss narrative (a third AI-GPU substrate supplier) and a below-consensus medium-term plan; a multiple de-rating can occur before it shows in reported earnings [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].
- **Principal limitation:** no revenue, net-profit or EPS consensus is available; only FY3/28 operating-profit consensus ([[190.0]]bn) is disclosed. Segment-level FY3/27 guidance is not disclosed by the company, and the broker note's segment table contains an internal inconsistency (Section 4).

---

## 2. Company and earnings structure

**How 4062.T makes money.** Two reportable segments plus "Others":

| H1 FY3/27 (Apr–Sep 2026) | Revenue (JPY m) | Segment profit (JPY m) | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electronics (IC package substrates) | 172,540 | 50,028 | 29.0% |
| Ceramics (DPF, EV battery, graphite) | 46,156 | 5,391 | 11.7% |
| Others | 43,849 | 4,623 | 10.5% |
| Adjustment | — | 73 | — |
| **Consolidated** | **262,546** | **60,116** | **22.9%** |

Source: [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.12]. Electronics is ~66% of revenue and ~83% of segment profit; it is the only segment that matters for valuation. Note that Electronics segment profit excludes JPY1,669m of depreciation on inactive assets, which is booked below the line as a non-operating expense [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.12]; on a fully-loaded basis the H1 Electronics margin is ~28.0%, not 29.0%.

**Revenue model and drivers.** Electronics sells semi-additive-process (SAP) IC package substrates to AI GPU, AI ASIC, server CPU and data-centre switch customers. Revenue is a function of *substrate area shipped* × price per unit area, and area is growing much faster than unit volumes: management estimates CY26→CY30 volume growth of 1.8x for GPU/ASIC and 1.3x for CPUs, but area-based demand growth of ~5.4x and ~2.5x respectively, because die sizes rise from 3.5 to 9+ reticles and layer counts from 9 to 14+ [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.14][doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1]. The company's aggregate SAP demand index rises from 100 in CY26 to 350 in CY30 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.12].

**Competitive position (evidence-based).** Management states it holds the top share in the high-end market and that the AI GPU substrate market is moving from a two-supplier structure (Ibiden plus one Taiwanese supplier) to three with a Korean entrant, but that aggregate competitor capacity will still fall far short of demand [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1]. Barriers cited are process know-how in SAP and embedded-bridge (EMIB/EMIB-T) construction, customer co-development (glass core substrates), and — critically — specialised engineering headcount, which management identifies as the binding constraint on new capacity, not buildings or equipment [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].

**Capital intensity and customer funding.** This is a customer-backed capacity model: advances received rose from JPY80,950m at 31 Mar 2026 to JPY199,746m at 30 Sep 2026, a JPY118,796m increase [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.5]. That is evidence of customer commitment to secure capacity; it is not evidence of permanent pricing power, and it flatters reported operating cash flow.

**Not disclosed / limitations.** Customer concentration, geographic revenue split, order backlog and contract structure are not disclosed in the available documents. Given the AI-accelerator end market, customer concentration is almost certainly high, but I will not estimate it.

---

## 3. Latest results and operating drivers

**Company-confirmed facts (H1 FY3/27, six months to 30 Sep 2026):**

- Revenue JPY262,546m (+34.3% YoY); operating profit JPY60,116m (+84.6%); ordinary profit JPY61,009m (+88.9%); net profit attributable to owners JPY38,574m (+74.8%) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1].
- Gross profit JPY97,705m on cost of sales JPY164,840m → gross margin 37.2%, versus 34.7% in H1 FY3/26 (JPY67,913m on JPY127,572m) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. SG&A rose only 6.4% to JPY37,589m, so essentially all of the margin expansion came from gross margin, not cost leverage below the gross line.
- Electronics segment profit JPY50,028m on revenue JPY172,540m (29.0%); Ceramics JPY5,391m on JPY46,156m (11.7%); Others JPY4,623m on JPY43,849m (10.5%) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.12].
- Depreciation and amortisation JPY35,877m, up from JPY25,429m [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9].
- Effective tax rate 34.5% (JPY20,490m on pre-tax JPY59,358m) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].
- Extraordinary loss of JPY1,650m, mainly loss on retirement of non-current assets (JPY1,606m) [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7].

**Management's stated explanation:** the driver was the Electronics business, "supported by favorable pricing and exceptionally strong demand for AI-related products"; Ceramics slightly beat plan on DPF backup parts and other products [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].

**Analyst interpretation (not company disclosure):** the Q2 sequential incremental margin was very high. Q2 revenue of [[139.3]]bn versus Q1 [[123.2]]bn is +13.1%, while Q2 operating profit of [[33.2]]bn versus Q1 [[26.9]]bn is +23.4%, implying an incremental operating margin of ~39% on the sequential revenue increase. That is consistent with premium-mix substrate revenue carrying high contribution margins at full utilisation, and it is the single most important number in the half: it tells you the marginal economics of the constrained capacity, not the average economics of the company.

**What changed in the period:** guidance was raised. FY3/27 revenue guidance is JPY565.0bn (+35.8%), operating profit JPY133.0bn (+114.4%), ordinary profit JPY134.5bn (+121.1%), net profit JPY89.0bn (+39.7%), EPS JPY157.17 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]. The interim dividend was raised from JPY15 to JPY20 per pre-split share (JPY10 post-split), and the full-year dividend is JPY20 post-split [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.2].

**Stock split — read every per-share figure with care.** 4062.T executed two 2-for-1 splits, effective 1 Jan 2026 and 1 Oct 2026, a cumulative 4x. All EPS and DPS figures in the tanshin are restated as if both splits occurred at the start of the prior fiscal year [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.1][p.13]. Pre-split FY3/27 guidance EPS would be JPY314.35 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]. Any comparison with pre-2026 per-share data is invalid without adjustment.

---

## 4. Management guidance and expectations

**FY3/27 guidance (company):** revenue JPY565.0bn, operating profit JPY133.0bn (23.5% margin), ordinary profit JPY134.5bn, net profit JPY89.0bn, EPS JPY157.17 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.3]. H2 implied: revenue JPY302.5bn, operating profit JPY72.9bn (24.1%), net profit JPY50.4bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].

**FY3/28 guidance (company, "medium-term plan"):** revenue unchanged at JPY650.0bn; operating profit raised from JPY150.0bn to JPY165.0bn; Electronics operating profit ~JPY144bn at ~31% margin [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. Note a conflict: JPM's note records the revised FY3/28 figure as JPY163.0bn, not JPY165.0bn [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. I use JPY165.0bn (two of three brokers and the model agree) and flag the JPY2bn discrepancy as unresolved.

**FY3/31 (FY2030) target:** unchanged at JPY1.0tn revenue and JPY300bn+ operating profit [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1]. Management explicitly states the new JPY151bn Cell 6 investment is *not* in these targets, i.e. it is upside [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].

**Key assumptions embedded in guidance:**
1. **Price declines.** Management deliberately embeds ASP erosion in FY3/27–FY3/30 guidance despite current tightness, on the argument that "it is dangerous to optimistically assume current peak pricing will last forever" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1]. GS estimates the FY3/28 price-decline drag at ~JPY10bn [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].
2. **Capacity.** Domestic high-end capacity index 100 in FY3/26 rising to 200 by FY3/30 (2x), against 4–5x market area demand [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1]. JPM records an intermediate path of 150 in FY3/28 and 200 in FY3/29 using its own fiscal labels [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]; the fiscal-year labelling between the transcript and the JPM note is not fully reconcilable, so I treat the intermediate path as indicative only.
3. **Depreciation.** JPY81.0bn in FY3/27 and JPY90.0bn in FY3/28, with the heavy step-up from FY3/29 as Cell 8 and Cell 6 exit construction-in-progress [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].
4. **Ceramics H2.** Operating profit of only JPY2.1bn in H2 versus JPY5.4bn in H1, on automotive sluggishness [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].

**External consensus:** only FY3/28 operating profit is disclosed, at ~JPY190bn per the Citi reference [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. Citi explicitly characterises management's JPY165bn as below consensus and reads the outlook as negative. No revenue, net-profit or EPS consensus is available — a genuine data gap, not evidence of mispricing.

**Unresolved conflict in the broker material.** JPM's segment table shows FY3/27 Electronics revenue of JPY385.0bn and operating profit of JPY141.0bn, i.e. a 36.6% margin [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. That is inconsistent with management's statement that the FY3/27 Electronics margin will be "approaching nearly 30%" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1], and it would imply an H2 Electronics margin above 40%. I do not use the JPY141bn figure; the conflict is most likely a transcription error in the broker note, but I cannot resolve it from the corpus.

---

## 5. Independent forecast

**FY3/27 (year to 31 Mar 2027):** revenue [[565.0]]bn, operating profit [[133.0]]bn ([[23.5]]% margin), net profit [[89.0]]bn, EPS [[157.2]] on the full-share count. This equals guidance by construction: H1 actual of [[262.5]]bn revenue and [[60.1]]bn operating profit plus H2 guidance of [[302.5]]bn and [[72.9]]bn. **There is no forecast edge for FY3/27** — the evidence does not support a different number, because the only two quarters of H2 are unobserved and management has just raised guidance on the back of a large H1 beat.

Quarterly build (model assumption, not guidance): Q3 revenue [[145.2]]bn / operating profit [[32.8]]bn / net profit [[20.2]]bn; Q4 [[157.3]]bn / [[40.1]]bn / [[30.2]]bn. The H2 split is an assumption based on prior-year Q4 skew and management's back-end-weighted commentary.

**FY3/28 (year to 31 Mar 2028):** revenue [[665.0]]bn, operating profit [[190.0]]bn ([[28.6]]% margin), net profit [[126.9]]bn, EPS [[224.1]]. This is above company guidance of JPY650.0bn/JPY165.0bn and equal to the Citi-cited consensus of [[190.0]]bn.

**Why the model differs from guidance for FY3/28 (one sentence):** the model reverses roughly JPY10bn of the price-decline buffer management has deliberately embedded, and adds stronger Cell 8 ramp, mix and utilisation than the company's cautious plan, which is the same reasoning three of the four brokers in the note use to argue guidance is conservative [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].

**FY3/29 (year to 31 Mar 2029):** revenue [[780.0]]bn, operating profit [[225.0]]bn ([[28.8]]%), net profit [[150.7]]bn, EPS [[266.1]]. This is beyond the decision horizon and rests on Cell 8 full ramp plus initial Cell 6 contribution; Cell 6 operations begin sequentially from FY2029 and management says contributions start in FY2030 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1], so the FY3/29 Cell 6 contribution in the model is small and appropriately so.

**Where I would push back on the model (Section 7 disagreement):**
1. **Q3 margin dip.** The model's Q3 operating profit of [[32.8]]bn is *below* Q2's [[33.2]]bn on higher revenue, implying a Q3 margin of 22.6% versus Q2's 23.8%. Management guides H2 to 24.1% with improving CPU/switch mix [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1], and the internal research note models Q3 at 24.5% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast p.1]. A Q3 dip is possible (start-up costs, Ceramics weakness) but it is an unsupported assumption, not a company signal. It does not change the full-year total, so it does not affect the investment conclusion.
2. **Share count.** The model uses 566.3m shares for EPS and 562.0m for market capitalisation. Post the 1 Oct 2026 split and the 1–21 Oct convertible conversion of JPY11.5bn face into 5,126,831 new shares, issued shares are 572,514,483 and net of 1,859,388 treasury shares ~570.7m [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.13]. On 570.7m shares, FY3/28 EPS would be ~222 rather than [[224.1]], and P/E ~36.2x rather than [[35.9]]x. This is a ~1% effect and does not change the conclusion, but the model's EPS is marginally overstated and its market cap marginally understated (Bloomberg market cap of JPY4,564.6bn at [[8,045]] implies 567.4m shares).
3. **Tax rate.** The model assumes 30% for FY3/28 and 32% for FY3/29. H1 FY3/27 ran at 34.5% [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.7]. If the higher rate persists, FY3/28 net profit would be ~JPY121bn rather than [[126.9]]bn — a ~5% EPS headwind. This is a real, if second-order, risk to the model's net profit and EPS.

---

## 6. Forecast bridges

**FY3/27 (H1 actual → full year):** revenue [[262.5]] + H2 guidance [[302.5]] = [[565.0]]; operating profit [[60.1]] + [[72.9]] = [[133.0]]; net profit [[38.6]] + [[50.4]] = [[89.0]]. This is arithmetic on guidance, not a forecast.

**FY3/27 → FY3/28 revenue:** base [[565.0]]; +[[80]] Cell 8 ramp and advanced-substrate volume; +[[30]] AI GPU/ASIC area growth and mix; −[[10]] product price declines (management's embedded assumption, broker-estimated at ~JPY10bn) = [[665.0]]. The two positive items are derived, not disclosed, and they overlap conceptually: Cell 8 volume and "area growth" both describe incremental substrate area sold. I flag this as a potential double count of up to ~JPY30bn of revenue; the honest reading is that the model needs ~JPY100bn of net volume/mix growth and has split it into two labels.

**FY3/27 → FY3/28 operating profit:** base [[133.0]]; +[[60]] incremental margin on higher advanced-substrate revenue (100.0 of revenue at ~60% incremental operating margin); −[[10]] price; −[[9]] depreciation increase (90.0 less 81.0); +[[16]] cost reduction and operating leverage (residual) = [[190.0]]. The 60% incremental margin is the single most aggressive assumption in the model. It is *not* the average margin (28.6%) and it is not the H1 sequential incremental margin (~39% at the group level, my calculation). It is defensible only if the incremental revenue is almost entirely premium AI substrate at full utilisation with no new depreciation — but the model separately charges JPY9bn of depreciation, so the 60% figure is effectively a pre-depreciation contribution margin. That is internally coherent but should be read as such. The [[16]] residual is a residual, not an operating driver.

**FY3/27 → FY3/28 net profit:** base [[89.0]]; +[[39.9]] after-tax operating profit increase (57.0 × 70%); −[[2]] non-operating and minority adjustment = [[126.9]]. The 30% tax rate is the weak link (see Section 5).

**FY3/28 → FY3/29:** revenue [[665.0]] +[[70]] Cell 8 full ramp/Cell 6 initial −[[15]] price +[[35]] AI area growth +[[25]] new capacity and mix = [[780.0]]; operating profit [[190.0]] +[[45]] volume −[[15]] price −[[20]] depreciation +[[25]] mix/productivity = [[225.0]]. The [[25]] mix/productivity item is a residual and is labelled as an assumption, not a driver.

---

## 7. Consensus and variant perception

**Where the forecast differs:** nowhere material. FY3/27 equals guidance; FY3/28 operating profit of [[190.0]]bn equals the Citi-cited consensus of [[190.0]]bn. **The base case does not currently provide a material forecast edge versus the available consensus for this metric.**

**Why:** the model's FY3/28 number is the consensus number, arrived at by reversing management's price buffer and adding Cell 8/mix. That is the same arithmetic the sell side has already done. The internal research note reaches the same JPY190bn and explicitly concludes that "the base forecast is no longer a differentiated bull call" [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast p.1].

**Where an edge could instead come from:**
- **Timing of the Cell 7/Cell 9 decision.** Management has committed to decide and disclose within FY3/27 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. Citi names this as the next catalyst; JPM notes full-scale mass production from those sites is not expected until FY2031 [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. An announcement is a sentiment event, not an earnings event, within the horizon.
- **A revised FY3/31 target.** Management says the FY2030 plan will be revisited once capex decisions are finalised, possibly at Q3 or full-year results [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. This is the most plausible positive surprise in the window.
- **Pricing.** Management concedes "greater-than-expected tailwinds at present" but refuses to extrapolate [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. If tightness persists into the FY3/28 negotiation round, the JPY10bn price-decline drag does not occur and FY3/28 operating profit moves toward JPY175bn on that item alone — still below consensus, so this is not an edge either.
- **Downside edge.** The share-loss narrative (third AI-GPU supplier) is a multiple risk that consensus operating-profit numbers do not capture. Citi explicitly warns that "the resulting decline in market share poses a risk of a temporary stock price correction" [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1].

## 8. Cash flow and balance sheet

**Operating cash flow quality.** H1 operating cash flow was JPY193,178m versus JPY36,697m a year earlier [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.9]. **Capex and free cash flow.** H1 purchases of property, plant and equipment were only JPY48,310m [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-semi-annual-tanshin p.10] against a full-year plan of ~JPY200bn [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1] (JPM records JPY210bn [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]). FY3/29 capex is guided above JPY400bn. **This business does not generate free cash flow during the build-out, and the model's valuation does not rest on FCF.**

Remaining CB face of ~JPY44.5bn is a continuing dilution overhang. ## 9. Valuation

**Method selection.** P/E on FY3/28 EPS and EV/EBITDA are the appropriate primary methods: the company is profitable, capital-intensive and in a capacity build, so P/E captures the earnings trajectory while EV/EBITDA neutralises the depreciation step-up that begins in FY3/29. FCF-based methods are not usable as a primary anchor because free cash flow is negative through the build. P/B is not informative for a business whose value is in process know-how and customer qualification rather than assets.

**P/E.** At [[8,045]] and FY3/28 EPS of [[224.1]], P/E is [[35.9]]x; on FY3/29 EPS of [[266.1]] it is 30.2x. On the post-conversion share count of ~570.7m, FY3/28 EPS is ~222 and P/E ~36.2x. The model's fair-value range of [[6,274]]–[[8,515]] brackets the current price; the base of [[8,000]] implies ~37x FY3/28 EPS, which is the multiple the internal research note also applies [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast p.1].

**EV/EBITDA.** FY3/28 EBITDA = operating profit [[190.0]] + depreciation 90.0 = ~JPY280bn. Market capitalisation JPY4,564.6bn less net cash ~JPY258bn = EV ~JPY4,306bn → ~15.4x. If net cash is consumed to ~JPY90bn by the capex programme, EV rises to ~JPY4,475bn → ~16.0x. Both are expensive for a capital-intensive manufacturer, even one with structural growth; the internal note reaches the same 16–17x conclusion [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast p.1].

**Sensitivity.** Each JPY10bn of FY3/28 operating profit is worth ~JPY7bn of net profit at a 30% tax rate, ~12 yen of EPS on 570.7m shares, and ~JPY440 per share at 36x — roughly 5.5% of the current price. The stock is therefore highly geared to the FY3/28 operating-profit outcome, which is precisely the number where the model has no edge over consensus.

**Why the framework is appropriate and what it does not capture.** The multiple embeds a scarcity premium for qualified advanced-substrate capacity. It does not capture the negative free cash flow, the dilution from the remaining convertible, or the possibility that a third AI-GPU supplier compresses the scarcity premium before it compresses earnings. Those are the reasons the fair-value range is wide ([[6,274]]–[[8,515]]) rather than a point.

1. **Q3 FY3/27 results (late Jan / early Feb 2027).** The first read on whether the H2 margin step-up to 24.1% is real. Watch group operating profit versus ~JPY33–36bn and Electronics margin versus 30%.

3. **Possible revision of the FY3/31 (FY2030) target**, which management says will be revisited once capex decisions are finalised, potentially at Q3 or full-year results [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. ## 11. Risks and invalidation conditions

**Business risk.** A third AI-GPU substrate supplier (Korean) entering a two-supplier market. Management argues aggregate competitor capacity still falls short of demand and that no meaningful share loss is expected [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1]; Citi warns the share-loss narrative alone can cause a temporary stock-price correction [doc-4062.T-brokers-views-oct-30-2026 p.1]. Both can be true: absolute shipments rise while the scarcity multiple compresses.

**Forecast risk.** The FY3/28 model depends on a 60% incremental operating margin on ~JPY100bn of incremental revenue and on a 30% tax rate versus 34.5% actual in H1. Both are assumptions, not evidence.

**Execution risk.** Cell 8 is the FY3/28 growth engine and starts sequentially from FY2027 [doc-4062.T-ibiden-co-ltd-company-presentation-20261030 p.13]. A delay hits revenue and depreciation absorption simultaneously. Management identifies specialised engineering headcount, not equipment, as the binding constraint, and says even a decision today would take a minimum of four years to reach mass production [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy3-2027-result-call p.1].

**Cash-flow and balance-sheet risk.** Capex of ~JPY350bn in FY3/28 and >JPY400bn in FY3/29 against EBITDA of ~JPY280bn means negative free cash flow for at least two years, funded by a shrinking net cash balance, customer advances and new debt. A demand air-pocket during the build would leave stranded, depreciating capacity.

**Valuation risk.** At [[35.9]]x FY3/28 EPS and ~15–16x EV/EBITDA with negative FCF, there is limited protection against an execution delay or an earnings miss. The stock is highly volatile (260-day volatility ~97% per Bloomberg).

**Regulatory / geopolitical risk.** Not addressed in the available documents. Currency: management's FY3/28 planning rate is not disclosed in the corpus; the internal note assumes ¥145/US$ and states the materials do not permit a reliable per-yen sensitivity [doc-4062.T-ibiden-q2-fy2027-results-forecast p.1]. **Thesis invalidation (observable):** Q3 group operating profit below ~JPY33bn; Electronics margin below 28%; a Cell 8 qualification slip disclosed by the company; evidence that the Korean entrant is winning AI-GPU allocation rather than adding incremental capacity; or a decision to fund Cell 7/9 without customer-backed terms.
